chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sulayman, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The supplication is answered for a man, then it is delayed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, (for) twenty years.'
ai.seo_question: How long can a supplication be delayed before its answer is realized?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while a supplicant may receive an immediate answer, the full realization or benefit of that dua can be deferred for up to twenty years. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'delayed response' (ta'khir) as a form of divine mercy, allowing time for spiritual maturation or the accumulation of greater reward, rather than a denial of the prayer.
